2.1.0 brings BitChord to Android, fixes the updater, and makes the macOS build easier to install.

## Android (new)
- A phone app of its own: bottom navigation (Home, Search, Library, Downloads), a mini player that opens Now Playing, the Back button, and the keyboard, all in Apple Music's look (SF Pro type and Apple's red) with your account's picture and name at the top.
- Music keeps playing with the app away, with a media notification (title, artist, artwork, previous / play-pause / next) and lock screen controls. The next song starts on its own.
- Sign in with Google or Spotify inside the app.
- Downloads: choose a folder once and every download is copied there. The first download asks for it.
- Music on this phone: add the folders you want (Japanese, English…), each its own collection. Only those folders are read, so ringtones and system sounds stay out.
- Spatial audio for headphones (Settings → Playback): a wider stage with a little room around it. It is a virtual surround for stereo songs, not head-tracked and not Dolby Atmos.
- A new Downloads page: where songs are saved, how much room they take, and your folders as coloured tiles.
- Shelves turn one page per swipe, and a vertical swipe over a shelf scrolls the page.

## Updates
- The updater now reads this repository's releases and the file names the release builds actually have. Copies installed before 2.1.0 still look at the old repository, so download 2.1.0 once by hand; from then on it updates itself.

## macOS
- A full icon set, and the install steps for macOS 15 (Privacy & Security → Open Anyway) are in the README.
- One Keychain item for your sign-in instead of several, so fewer access prompts. Sign-ins from earlier versions still read.
- yt-dlp finds Homebrew's Node when the app is opened from Finder.

## Known issues
- Android: Better Lyrics isn't available yet; the other lyrics sources work. Opening the app from its icon after its screen was closed from the recent apps list restarts it, which stops the music for a moment.
- Android: the first build is for 64-bit ARM phones (Android 8 or newer).
- The macOS build is signed ad hoc, not notarized, so macOS asks you to allow it once.
